svg.text: Figure 1a — Runtime Architecture and Threat Overview
Juice Shop · 20.1.1 · 7 components · 17 data flows · 7 trust boundaries · 59 threats in the model

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-01; tb-2 External → C-03; tb-11 C-01 → External; tb-12 C-04 → External
Trust boundary crossing: tb-8 C-01 → C-06; tb-9 C-02 → C-06; tb-10 C-01 → C-07

df-002: Anonymous REST API calls — product catalog, search, registration, public challenge metadata — no authentication required (HTTPS) df-003: Authenticated REST API calls — basket, orders, cards, addresses — JWT Bearer required via isAuthorized (HTTPS) df-002 authentication: No authentication enforced on public routes such as GET /api/Products and POST /api/Users (server.ts:408); evidence: server.ts:408 df-002 access group: Anonymous vs authenticated API; alternatives; step n/a df-003 authentication: RS256 JWT verified via express-jwt isAuthorized() middleware (lib/insecurity.ts:156); token originally issued by authorize() (lib/insecurity.ts:54); evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:156, frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:16 df-003 access group: Anonymous vs authenticated API; alternatives; step n/a

df-004: User login POST to /rest/user/login — email and MD5-hashed password; raw SQL injection sink (HTTPS) df-005: 2FA TOTP verification — temporary bearer token plus TOTP code submitted to /rest/2fa/verify for enrolled accounts (HTTPS) df-004 authentication: Email and password submitted as JSON body; password compared via unsalted MD5 in raw SQL (routes/login.ts:34); evidence: routes/login.ts:34, server.ts:596 df-004 access group: Credentials (2FA if enrolled); sequence; step 1 df-005 authentication: Temporary JWT token issued at step 1 of login, passed to 2FA endpoint (server.ts:458); evidence: server.ts:458 df-005 access group: Credentials (2FA if enrolled); sequence; step 2

df-006: Password reset — security question answer submitted to reset password; account recovery method (HTTPS) df-006 authentication: Security question answer used for account recovery; no secondary factor (routes/resetPassword.ts:1); evidence: routes/resetPassword.ts:16

df-007: Socket.IO connection for challenge notifications and CTF updates; no auth check evidenced (WebSocket) df-007 authentication: No authentication check; confirmed by T-038 (evidence-verified); evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:23

df-008: Sequelize ORM and raw SQL queries — users, products, orders, cards, addresses via SQLite (SQL) df-008 authentication: In-process embedded SQLite via Sequelize; no network authentication (models/index.ts:34); evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-009: Login credential query — raw SQL from interpolated email and MD5-hashed password (SQL) df-009 authentication: In-process embedded SQLite; no network authentication (routes/login.ts:34); evidence: routes/login.ts:34

df-010: MarsDB in-process document queries for product reviews and user memories (in-process) df-010 authentication: In-process MarsDB; no network authentication (data/mongodb.ts:1); evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9

df-011: LLM chat inference to OpenAI-compatible endpoint via @ai-sdk/openai-compatible; streaming (HTTPS) df-011 authentication: API key for OpenAI-compatible endpoint via @ai-sdk/openai-compatible (routes/chat.ts:9); evidence: routes/chat.ts:9

df-012: Ethereum JSON-RPC calls to Alchemy Sepolia endpoint — NFT minting verification and wallet exploit address validation (HTTPS) df-012 authentication: Alchemy RPC endpoint key embedded in provider URL (routes/nftMint.ts:18); evidence: routes/nftMint.ts:18

df-013: Server-side fetch to user-controlled profile image URL; caller-controlled destination (HTTP) df-013 authentication: No authentication on outbound request; target URL is user-controlled (routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts:24); evidence: routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts:24
Internet Attacker → C-01 · Express REST API Server: scenario 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; its findings also affect C-02 · Authentication and Session Management, C-04 · Web3 / NFT / Wallet Surface
Internet Attacker → C-02 · Authentication and Session Management: scenario 2, 4
Internet Attacker → C-04 · Web3 / NFT / Wallet Surface: scenario 2
Internet Attacker → Juice Shop User: scenario 6, 7
Further capabilities: XML parsing — evidence: lib/xml.ts:35; Server-side templates — evidence: server.ts:139

Anonymous or authenticated end user operating the Angular SPA in a browser. The open self-registration endpoint means any internet visitor can become an authenticated user immediately.
Google OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authorization server used by the Angular SPA for browser-only implicit-flow sign-in. No server-side OAuth code path exists; the frontend handles the token directly.
g.text: server used by the Angular SPA for

g.title: Configurable OpenAI-compatible LLM inference endpoint (defaults to local Ollama). Called by the Express API via the @ai-sdk/openai-compatible SDK for the chatbot feature. Endpoint URL and API key are runtime configuration.
Alchemy JSON-RPC endpoint for Ethereum Sepolia testnet. Called by the Web3/NFT routes to verify NFT minting status and wallet exploit addresses.
Application role with elevated rights, evidenced by its access check.
Server-side fetch to user-controlled profile image URL; caller-controlled destination

Google OAuth 2.0 df-014: Google OAuth implicit-flow redirect — browser redirects to accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth to initiate sign-in (HTTPS); Implicit flow authorization request; no client secret or PKCE (frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:31) df-015: OAuth implicit-flow token delivery — redirect back to SPA with access token in URL fragment (HTTPS); ID/access token delivered in URL fragment to the SPA; missing state validation (frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:58) df-016: OAuth profile request (HTTPS); The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request

C-05 · Angular SPA Frontend df-014: Google OAuth implicit-flow redirect — browser redirects to accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth to initiate sign-in (HTTPS); Implicit flow authorization request; no client secret or PKCE (frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:31) df-015: OAuth implicit-flow token delivery — redirect back to SPA with access token in URL fragment (HTTPS); ID/access token delivered in URL fragment to the SPA; missing state validation (frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:58) df-016: OAuth profile request (HTTPS); The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE-per-element: filled = threats found in that class
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
LLM + tools = model calls with executable application tools
URL fetch = requests a URL that runtime input selects or influences
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Matching E-labels indicate a connection; lines omitted.
Stored script execution yields server code control
The recipient performs no authentication check on this connection.
The recipient checks the supplied password.
The recipient checks the token supplied with the request.
The caller presents a configured service credential.
Delegated access; only the evidenced protocol step is covered.
Security question answer used for account recovery; no secondary
Numbered hexagon: authentication · circle: attack scenario
Red: absent / unsafe · yellow: standard / limited · green: stronger
Method properties, not proof of a secure implementation.
Components are ordered within their layer to reduce line crossings, not by
